claims.text: Local compositional fluctuations in single-phase multi-component concentrated alloys cause severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion forces edge-dislocation cores to deviate from their neutral planes.
Deviation of edge-dislocation cores from their neutral planes produces wavy dislocation lines.
Wavy edge-dislocation configurations reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility caused by wavy dislocations enhances yield strength.
The target initial state is a single-phase BCC concentrated alloy.
The target initial state has significant compositional fluctuations and associated lattice distortions.
Post-solidification homogenization can reduce local compositional fluctuations and severe lattice distortion.
The proposed processing can reduce compositional fluctuations without introducing secondary phases.
Reducing compositional fluctuations and lattice distortion makes dislocations more mobile.
Reducing lattice distortion will lower yield strength relative to the conventionally processed baseline.
Reducing lattice distortion will transform wavy edge-dislocation behavior into more conventional dislocation configurations.
The baseline alloy has a dominant edge-dislocation mechanism responsible for its high yield strength.
The relevant alloy can retain a single BCC phase from room temperature to elevated temperatures.
The proposed mechanism should apply when secondary-phase precipitation and grain-boundary effects are minimal.
Processing-induced secondary-phase formation can alter mechanical properties and therefore must be isolated as a confounder.
Elastic isotropy or related elastic properties may shift after lattice distortion is reduced.
The magnitude of the strength and dislocation-response changes may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
